1	// Command git-remote-entire is the git remote helper for entire:// URLs.
2	//
3	// Git resolves `git clone entire://host/project/repo` by exec'ing a binary
4	// named git-remote-entire on PATH, handing it the remote-helper protocol on
5	// stdin and reading responses from stdout. This is a small, dedicated
6	// binary (no cobra command tree) that shares the protocol, transport, and
7	// auth packages with the main entire CLI.
8	//
9	// IMPORTANT: nothing here may write to stdout except the helper protocol
10	// itself — git parses stdout as a strict pkt-line stream, so a stray banner
11	// or log line corrupts the transfer. Diagnostics go to stderr (and the
12	// ENTIRE_DEBUG-gated debuglog).
13	//
14	// Authentication resolves the login context for the target cluster from the
15	// shared contexts.json: the cluster's cores come from the cluster_cores.json
16	// cache (or a live /.well-known fetch on miss), then the account is selected
17	// from local contexts. It then mints a jurisdiction access token by
18	// exchanging that context's login JWT (or ENTIRE_TOKEN in CI).
19	package main
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"errors"
24		"fmt"
25		"io"
26		"net/http"
27		"net/url"
28		"os"
29		"os/signal"
30		"regexp"
31		"runtime"
32		"strings"
33		"syscall"
34		"time"
35	
36		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth"
37		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo"
38		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery"
39		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/httpclient"
40		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/httputil"
41		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/userdirs"
42		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper"
43		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/debuglog"
44		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/githelper"
45		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/httpdebug"
46		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/replicas"
47		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/transport"
48	)
49	
50	func main() {
51		os.Exit(run(os.Args))
52	}
53	
54	func run(args []string) int {
55		// --version / --help only activate as the sole argument (so os.Args has
56		// length 2). Git always invokes the helper as
57		// `git-remote-entire <remote-name> <url>` (os.Args length 3), so these can
58		// never collide with a real remote-helper invocation.
59		if len(args) == 2 {
60			if text, ok := infoFlagText(args[1], loadedVersion()); ok {
61				fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, text)
62				return 0
63			}
64		}
65	
66		if len(args) < 3 {
67			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "usage: %s <remote-name> <url>\n", remotehelper.BinaryName)
68			return 128
69		}
70	
71		// Build info drives the identifier the helper advertises upstream.
72		// One string covers both surfaces:
73		//   - githelper.Agent rides in the git protocol pkt-line agent=
74		//     capability appended to upload-pack / receive-pack / v2 requests.
75		//   - httpUserAgent rides in the HTTP User-Agent header on every
76		//     outbound request so server access logs can attribute traffic.
77		// Using the same value keeps the two log surfaces correlatable.
78		versioninfo.Load()
79		helperAgent := remotehelper.BinaryName + "/" + versioninfo.Version
80		githelper.Agent = helperAgent
81		httpUserAgent := helperAgent
82	
83		rawURL := args[2]
84		parsedURL, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
85		switch {
86		case err != nil:
87			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: invalid URL %q: %v\n", rawURL, err)
88			return 128
89		case parsedURL.Scheme != "entire":
90			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: unsupported URL scheme %q (expected 'entire')\n", parsedURL.Scheme)
91			return 128
92		case parsedURL.Host == "":
93			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: missing host in URL %q\n", rawURL)
94			return 128
95		}
96	
97		ctx, stop := installSignals()
98		defer stop()
99	
100		skipTLS := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY") == "true"
101	
102		nodeCfg := replicas.Resolve(parsedURL)
103	
104		// This client drives the auth path only: cluster /.well-known discovery
105		// and the token exchange. Both talk to a single control-plane host with no
106		// failover to fall back on, so they get the patient discovery dial budget
107		// (DiscoveryDialTimeout, i.e. DefaultDiscoveryDialTimeout unless
108		// ENTIRE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS overrides it) rather than the short failover
109		// one — a slow cold connect here would otherwise fail the whole clone/fetch.
110		httpClient := &http.Client{
111			Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
112			Transport: &httpclient.UserAgentTransport{
113				Next: &httpdebug.TimingRoundTripper{
114					Next:  httpclient.NewDiscoveryTransport(skipTLS),
115					Label: "auth",
116				},
117				UA: httpUserAgent,
118			},
119		}
120	
121		creds, err := resolveCreds(ctx, parsedURL, skipTLS, httpClient)
122		if err != nil {
123			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: %v\n", err)
124			return 128
125		}
126	
127		setAuth := func(req *http.Request) error {
128			// Refuse to attach credentials to a request we can't classify as a
129			// known git smart-HTTP endpoint. The jurisdiction token doesn't
130			// need the action, but sending a bearer to an unexpected endpoint
131			// is never right.
132			action := gitActionFromRequest(req)
133			if action == "" {
134				return fmt.Errorf("refusing to attach credentials: %s %s is not a recognised git smart-HTTP endpoint", req.Method, req.URL.Path)
135			}
136			start := time.Now()
137			token, err := creds.Token(req.Context())
138			if err != nil {
139				return fmt.Errorf("git credential exchange: %w", err)
140			}
141			debuglog.Printf("timing: token-acquire action=%s dur_ms=%d (keychain + login refresh + exchange; ~0 when memoized)", action, time.Since(start).Milliseconds())
142			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
143			return nil
144		}
145	
146		var onNodeFailed func(string)
147		if nodeCfg.Caching() {
148			onNodeFailed = func(string) { replicas.Invalidate(nodeCfg.ClusterHost, nodeCfg.RepoPath) }
149		}
150	
151		proxy := transport.New(transport.Config{
152			Nodes:   nodeCfg,
153			Path:    parsedURL.Path,
154			SkipTLS: skipTLS,
155			SetAuth: setAuth,
156			// A 401 means the data plane rejected the credential itself (e.g.
157			// signing-key rotation invalidated a persisted jurisdiction token) —
158			// drop it so the next invocation re-mints instead of failing until
159			// the token's recorded expiry. The env-token source persists
160			// nothing; it drops only its in-process memo.
161			OnUnauthorized: creds.Invalidate,
162			OnNodeFailed:   onNodeFailed,
163			UserAgent:      httpUserAgent,
164		})
165	
166		protocolVersion := resolveProtocolVersion()
167		debuglog.Printf("git protocol.version=%d (v2 advertises stateless-connect + push; v0/v1 advertises connect)", protocolVersion)
168	
169		helperStart := time.Now()
170		if err := githelper.Run(ctx, proxy, protocolVersion, os.Stdin, os.Stdout); err != nil {
171			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, fatalMessage(err, parsedURL))
172			return 128
173		}
174		debuglog.Printf("timing: helper-session dur_ms=%d", time.Since(helperStart).Milliseconds())
175		return 0
176	}
177	
178	// wrongClusterRe extracts the host that actually serves the repo from the
179	// data plane's `invalid_target` error_description (RFC 8693). The data plane
180	// emits this when the audience host doesn't host the repo but a sibling
181	// cluster does, naming the correct host so we can point the user at it. The
182	// phrasing is "… it lives on \"<host>\" …"; anchoring on "lives on" keeps the
183	// match tied to this specific, actionable case rather than other
184	// invalid_target variants (e.g. a suspended mirror).
185	var wrongClusterRe = regexp.MustCompile(`lives on "([^"]+)"`)
186	
187	// fatalMessage renders the stderr "fatal: …" line for a transfer error. When
188	// the failure is the data plane reporting that the repo lives on a different
189	// cluster, it special-cases the raw OAuth chain into an actionable message
190	// naming the correct host (and the corrected entire:// URL). Everything else
191	// falls back to the verbatim error.
192	func fatalMessage(err error, parsedURL *url.URL) string {
193		var oe *httputil.OAuthError
194		if errors.As(err, &oe) && oe.Code == "invalid_target" {
195			if m := wrongClusterRe.FindStringSubmatch(oe.Description); m != nil {
196				host := m[1]
197				// Copy the URL the user typed and swap only the host, so any
198				// escaped path (RawPath) or query stays byte-identical to what
199				// they originally ran.
200				correctedURL := *parsedURL
201				correctedURL.Scheme = "entire"
202				correctedURL.Host = host
203				correctedURL.User = nil
204				corrected := correctedURL.String()
205				return fmt.Sprintf("fatal: this repository is not hosted on %s; it lives on %s.\n"+
206					"Re-run against the correct host, e.g.:\n\n    git clone %s\n",
207					parsedURL.Host, host, corrected)
208			}
209		}
210		return fmt.Sprintf("fatal: %v\n", err)
211	}
212	
213	// loadedVersion populates the build info and returns the resolved version.
214	func loadedVersion() string {
215		versioninfo.Load()
216		return versioninfo.Version
217	}
218	
219	// infoFlagText renders the output for the standalone --version / --help flags,
220	// returning false for anything else. Kept pure (version passed in, no globals)
221	// so it's unit-testable.
222	func infoFlagText(flag, version string) (string, bool) {
223		switch flag {
224		case "--version":
225			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\nGo version: %s\nOS/Arch: %s/%s\n",
226				remotehelper.BinaryName, version, runtime.Version(), runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH), true
227		case "--help":
228			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\n\n"+
229				"This is a helper which Git calls when encountering entire://... URLs.  "+
230				"For more information see https://github.com/entireio/cli.\n",
231				remotehelper.BinaryName, version), true
232		}
233		return "", false
234	}
235	
236	// resolveProtocolVersion reads the effective protocol.version from
237	// the GIT_PROTOCOL environment variable. The value is a colon-
238	// separated list of key=value pairs (e.g. "version=2"). We accept
239	// 0, 1, or 2; any other value emits a stderr warning and falls
240	// back to 2 — upstream Git's default since 2.26.
241	func resolveProtocolVersion() int {
242		return parseProtocolVersion(os.Getenv("GIT_PROTOCOL"), os.Stderr)

Confirmed valid. `mirrorCloneRefRe` is anchored `^/?gh/<owner>/<repo>$`, so a partial shorthand like `/gh` or `/gh/owner` is rejected by `entire repo clone`. Both bots caught a real defect:

- **The bug:** the forge-in-host branch unconditionally suggests `entire repo clone /<host><path>`. For `entire://gh` it emits `entire repo clone /gh`, and for `entire://gh/owner` it emits `/gh/owner` — both invalid refs that fail immediately. Worse, the empty-host branch (using `strings.Cut` with an `ok` guard) *does* fall back correctly for `entire:///gh`, so the two equivalent mistakes are handled inconsistently — exactly as Cursor noted.

The fix: only emit the clone hint when the reconstructed shorthand is a complete `forge/owner/repo` triple. This also lets me collapse the two branches and inline `clusterHostHint` (now a single call site). Let me apply it.

func missingClusterHostMessage(parsedURL *url.URL, rawURL string) string {
	// Forge id in the host slot: the shorthand is /<host><path>.
	if gitremote.IsSupportedForge(parsedURL.Host) {
		return clusterHostHint(parsedURL.Host, "/"+parsedURL.Host+parsedURL.Path)
	}
	// Empty host with a forge-led path: the path is already the shorthand.
	if forge, _, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimPrefix(parsedURL.Path, "/"), "/"); ok && gitremote.IsSupportedForge(forge) {
		return clusterHostHint(forge, parsedURL.Path)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("fatal: missing host in URL %q\n", rawURL)
}

// clusterHostHint is the actionable message pointing a host-less entire:// URL
// at the `entire repo clone` picker, which resolves the mirror for the given
// forge shorthand.
func clusterHostHint(forge, shorthand string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf(
		"fatal: entire:// URL is missing its cluster host (%q is a forge id, not a host).\n"+
			"The full form is entire://<cluster-host>/%s/<owner>/<repo>.\n"+
			"To pick a mirror interactively, run:\n\n    entire repo clone %s\n",
		forge, forge, shorthand)
}

The PR is updated. Here's my review of the comments and what I did about them.

## The comments

Two automated reviewers ran — **Cursor Bugbot** and **GitHub Copilot** — and both landed on the **same single, valid issue** (no human comments yet):

> `missingClusterHostMessage` suggested `entire repo clone` for *any* forge id in the host slot, without checking that owner **and** repo were present. So `entire://gh` produced the hint `entire repo clone /gh`, and `entire://gh/owner` produced `/gh/owner` — refs that `parseMirrorCloneRef` (`^/?gh/<owner>/<repo>$`) rejects immediately. Worse, the *empty-host* branch already fell back correctly, so `entire://gh/owner` and `entire:///gh/owner` — the same mistake — behaved inconsistently.

I verified this against `repo_clone.go:24` (`mirrorCloneRefRe`): the ref must be a complete `gh/<owner>/<repo>` triple. The finding is correct — a genuine "helpful command that fails immediately" defect. Everything else in the reviews was just the overview/boilerplate (Cursor's "Fix in Cursor" links, Copilot's file summary).

## The fix (pushed as `6050a60b3`)

- Reworked `missingClusterHostMessage` to reconstruct the intended shorthand once (forge-in-host-slot *or* empty-host both normalize to `forge/owner/repo`), then emit the `entire repo clone` hint **only when it's a complete 3-segment triple with a supported forge**. Anything shorter (`entire://gh`, `.../owner`), longer (extra segments), or non-forge falls back to the plain `missing host` error. This also fixes the inconsistency between the two URL shapes.
- Collapsing the two branches let me inline the now-single-use `clusterHostHint`.
- Added the 4 regression cases Copilot explicitly asked for: `entire://gh`, `entire://gh/owner`, `entire:///gh/owner`, and a too-many-segments path — all 9 test cases pass.

The PR and all git operations live in `cli_experiments_2` (the working dir); my initial grep this turn accidentally hit the other checkout, which briefly looked like the change was missing.
